cards.title: Radar brightness: HH and HV
body: NISAR's radar "sends out a pulse of energy" and "records the amount of that energy reflected back after it interacts with Earth". In the HH and HV images, brighter means more energy came back.
H is horizontal and V is vertical. A signal "emitted in horizontal (H) and received in horizontal (H) would be indicated HH". HV is the cross-polarized channel.
HH is most sensitive to double bounce, from buildings, tree trunks, or inundated vegetation. HV is most sensitive to volume scattering, from leaves and branches in a forest canopy.
cards.weInfer: HH helps pick out the city's buildings, and HV helps pick out vegetation.

cards.title: Radar shows vs. we infer
body: Every place card splits its text in two. "Radar shows" is only what the measurement says: how bright the radar return was, or how far the ground moved along the radar's line of sight. "We infer" is our reading of why, worded as a hypothesis. We keep them apart so you can see where the data ends and our interpretation begins.

cards.title: Provisional data
body: These images use NISAR PROVISIONAL products, which are calibrated and validated at only a limited set of sites so far.
Ground motion is measured along the radar's line of sight, relative to a reference area in the western hills, not straight down.

sources.title: Our analysis of 27 NISAR GUNW pairs (PROVISIONAL), track 19 / frame 11, Nov 2025 to Oct 2026
